back: The continuous collection and analysis of information about a business's internal and external environment, so that managers can spot changes early and plan a response.
Strengths and weaknesses (internal) and opportunities and threats (external) sorted into a framework to support a strategy.
PEST: political, economic, social, technological. PESTEL adds environmental and legal.
Internal: staff, finance, skills, equipment (controllable). External: economy, law, technology, competitors (can only be responded to).
Rivalry among firms, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of buyers and of suppliers: the stronger the forces, the lower the profit in the industry.
Match strengths to opportunities, use strengths against threats, fix weaknesses that block opportunities, and avoid weaknesses meeting threats.
Many equal-sized firms, slow market growth, similar products and high fixed costs.
SWOT is subjective and dates quickly; PEST is a checklist without priorities; five forces suits established industries and needs industry-wide knowledge.
The same external change can be both: a rise in fuel prices threatens a transport operator but creates an opportunity for a solar lighting supplier.
